content.text: {"relation":"REFINED","consensus_summary":"Worship is reverent adoration, homage, and total self-surrender directed exclusively to God — ascribing supreme worth ('worth-ship') to Him, expressed outwardly in bowing/prostration (shachah/proskuneo) and inwardly in whole-life submission and service. Expressions include praise, prayer, singing, sacrifice, obedience, and corporate liturgy; the main disputes concern scope (ritual vs. whole-life vs. experiential encounter), not the core.","book_summary":"Worship is to bow down and serve — bodily homage joined with lived allegiance, the visible fear of the LORD, offered at God's appointed times and on His terms. The book explicitly denies that worship is the song service, noting Scripture distinguishes worship from singing within single scenes (e.g., 2 Chr 20:18-19).","consensus_core_identification":"Exclusive homage and self-surrender to God alone — ascribing supreme worth through bowing, service, praise, and whole-life devotion.","book_core_identification":"Bowing down plus serving God alone — bodily homage and lived allegiance on God's terms, expressly excluding singing/praise from the category of worship.","core_relation":"BOOK_NARROWS","extension_relation":"BOOK_SUBSET","boundary_disagreement":"The book excludes sung praise and the 'song service' from worship, whereas most consensus responses include praise, singing, and musical expression as legitimate (even central) forms of worship — while themselves criticizing the reduction of worship to music. The book also adds a condition the consensus does not stress: worship must occur 'at His appointed times, on His terms.' The book reclassifies singing/praise as an adjacent but distinct activity (as in 2 Chr 20:18-19 where Judah worships by bowing while the Levites separately stand to praise).","material_contradiction":"","rationale":"The book retains the consensus's central referent: exclusive homage and service to God alone, expressed in bodily prostration and life allegiance (Ex 20:5; Matt 4:10 are staple consensus proof texts). Its 'bow down and serve' formula matches the shachah/proskuneo + latreuo core the consensus itself identifies, and even resembles Response D's minority 'strictly prostration/homage' alternative. However, the book materially tightens the boundary by expelling singing/praise from the category — cases the consensus admits as common expressions of worship — and by adding the 'appointed times, on His terms' condition. This is genuine boundary disagreement without replacing the referent, so REFINED rather than DIVERGENT. Notably, several consensus responses already flag 'worship = music' as a criticized reduction, so the book radicalizes an existing consensus tendency rather than contradicting the core.","citation_support":"PARTIAL","strongest_objection":"One could argue for MATCH: the consensus itself defines worship etymologically as bowing/prostration plus service and criticizes equating worship with singing, so the book's entry merely sharpens an emphasis already present (especially Response D's prostration alternative). But the book's categorical exclusion of the song service, plus the added 'appointed times, on His terms' condition, rejects cases mainstream treatments admit, which is more than immaterial wording. Conversely, the 'appointed times' clause is unsupported by the printed verses, which is why citation support is only partial despite 2 Chr 20:18-19 strongly backing the worship/singing distinction.","confidence":"high"}
